unit: City of Miami building permit + county Class I
qualifier: Miami's code says no waterfront structure may be built, rebuilt or repaired without a Building Department permit, and the application must include the county's preliminary environmental approval. Most repairs also need a Miami-Dade DERM Class I permit, which the county requires for work in tidal waters in every city; sealing cracks and repairing pilasters are exempt. Repairs that reach the city's 50% substantial-repair threshold must meet its 6 ft NAVD88 minimum height (4 ft on the Miami River, built to be raised 2 ft).

every job needs signed and sealed plans, a survey under one year old and a cost estimate backed by an executed contract; work of $5,000 or more also needs a top-of-wall survey with elevations no more than 10 ft apart - Sec. 29-84 | Height :: Minimum 6 ft NAVD88 (Miami River and tributaries: 4 ft NAVD88, built to be raised 2 ft) for new work and substantial improvements - Sec. 29-89(a)(4) | Substantial repair :: Repairs to 50% or more of the wall length, costing 50% or more of a new wall, or changing elevation along 50% or more of the length must meet current elevation and design standards for the length of the property - Sec. 29-89(a)(5) | Fees :: A repair permit costs $90 or 10% of the repair cost up to $525, whichever is greater; meeting the deadlines entitles the owner to full mitigation of fines - Sec. 29-95 | Hardship :: The city manager's designee may waive some or all city permit fees for an owner required to repair a failing seawall who shows extreme financial hardship - Sec. 29-83 | County Class I permit :: Miami-Dade DERM must issue a Class I permit before any work in, on, over or upon tidal waters anywhere in the county, including inside cities - County Code Sec. 24-48(1)(d) and 24-48.1(1)(a) | Short form :: Rebuilding or repairing a seawall at the mean high water line or no more than 18 inches waterward of the existing wall qualifies for a short-form application. unit: city Public Works permit (code requires Commission approval) + county Class I

Its code says every Class 2 application, which covers seawalls, needs City Commission approval after a public hearing; whether a routine repair goes to the Commission in practice is not confirmed. Most repairs also need a Miami-Dade DERM Class I permit, which the county requires for work in tidal waters in every city; sealing cracks and repairing pilasters are exempt.

Most standard-form applications are now decided by the Director, apart from listed exceptions such as variances - Sec. 24-48.2(I)(B)(1)(iii)-(iv) and (II)(C)(1), as amended by Ord. 25-73 (1 July 2025) | County clock :: Ord. 25-73 Sec. 8 directs the County to issue a Completeness Summary within 10 calendar days of submission and a final decision on short-form seawall applications within 90 calendar days after that summary. The applicant may waive these limits in writing. The County Mayor reported the timeframes apply from 1 Dec 2025 (report to the Commission dated 17 Apr 2026) | No Class I needed :: Sealing cracks and spalls on the cap or face, repairing pilasters, backfilling behind the wall, and limited riprap or sand-cement bags at the toe (no more than 2 ft out) - Sec. 24-48(3)(b)-(f) | Quick approval instead :: Repairing or replacing the cap or the tieback system gets a written expedited administrative authorization, answered within 10 business days, if the contractor submits structurally approved plans from the building authority - Sec. 24-48(4)(f)-(g) | Not a substitute :: A county permit does not relieve the applicant from obtaining all required federal, state and local permits - Sec. 24-48.5(1) | State (FDEP) :: No state environmental permit is needed to restore a seawall at its previous location, upland of it, or within 18 inches waterward of it - Fla. Stat. 403.813(1)(e). Stat. 403.813(1) | Federal (Army Corps) :: A Department of the Army permit is required for structures or work in or affecting navigable waters, either under a nationwide or regional general permit or an individual permit - 33 CFR 322.3(a)

unit: village building permit + county Class I
qualifier: Miami Shores requires a development permit for seawall work, and its dock and seawall checklist says plans must be approved by DERM. Most repairs also need a Miami-Dade DERM Class I permit, which the county requires for work in tidal waters in every city; sealing cracks and repairing pilasters are exempt. Substantial repairs must bring the wall to 4 ft NAVD88 along the whole property.
